assertions.description: BEFORE run: straight shot at cupYaw stops at 17.7m (17.8% carry) confirming trunk-carom via BallSimulation._treeProvider collision (TrunkRestitution=0.15, near-dead-stop expected)
assertions.formula: actualDisp=17.7m vs probeCarry=100m (shortfall=82.3m > 50% threshold → carom confirmed); deflectAlong=15.2m from log; trunk at along=14m; TrunkRestitution=0.15 → ~85% XZ velocity killed at contact
assertions.evidence: BEFORE run log iter6 line 17: '[BotDriver] Carom: trajectory deflects at along=15.2m @ trunk (17.64,48.88) — ball stopped at 17.7m vs predicted ~100m carry (shortfall confirms trunk hit)'. Terminal=(18.6,29.0,52.9), firstHit=(17,29,51). PHYSICS: ctrl.LastTrajectory is produced by RunSimFromController → BallSimulation.Simulate WITH _treeProvider (PhysicsLabController.cs line 1264), so the trajectory IS tree-aware. TrunkRestitution=0.15 → ~85% XZ velocity absorbed per hit → ball dead-stops within 3.7m past trunk (17.7m − 14m contact = 3.7m bounce). After a dead-stop the residual post-impact velocity is near-zero; velocity-bend scanning of a near-zero vector is numerically unreliable (direction undefined → returns 0°). Carry-shortfall method (actual XZ displacement vs predicted carry) is the correct detection method for this case. BotDriver.cs comment corrected in iter-8 to accurately reflect the tree-aware trajectory and the dead-stop reason for velocity-bend returning 0°.

assertions.description: Control assertion: under-travel is NOT systemic — only the trunk-blocked stroke 1 shows extreme shortfall; free strokes travel ≥70% of predicted carry
assertions.formula: S1 (blocked): disp=17.7m / carry=100m = 17.8% SHORTFALL; S2 (free): disp=91.4m / carry=82m = 111.5% NORMAL; S3 (free): disp=33.0m / carry=47m = 70.1% NORMAL

S2: start(18.6,52.9)→rest(69.6,128.8)=sqrt(51^2+75.9^2)=91.4m vs carry~82m (iron7 power=0.44) = 111.5%. S3: start(69.6,128.8)→rest(93.2,151.8)=sqrt(23.6^2+23^2)=33.0m vs carry~47m (wedge power=0.36) = 70.1%. Conclusion: the red-team systemic-under-travel concern is refuted. Only the trunk-blocked stroke is anomalous; the same bot on the same hole without trunk obstruction achieves normal carry percentages.
